assessments.zone: Wikong health zone villages (Kayind/Masol, Kapat, Kakang, Mansonj, Mbangom, Mukatshiot, Ntikit, Tshibal, Katambal, Mpund)
assessments.evidence: Remote rural health zone with no reported armed-group presence; the Kamuina Nsapu insurgency of 2016-2018 did not establish lasting control here. Day-to-day order rests on Lunda customary chiefs with sparse PNC posts as the state's coercive presence.

assessments.zone: Rural settlements and smaller towns of Luputa, Kanda Kanda and Kalenda secteurs (incl. Kamanda Kadila/Kanda-Kanda, Fuabana, Tshinguluiba, Kasongo, Mbayi Museng)
assessments.evidence: Rural Kasai-Lomami savanna area with no known armed-group presence; order is kept by customary chiefs with PNC posts at secteur and groupement centres. Occasional customary disputes and banditry do not amount to armed-group control.

assessments.zone: Luputa town and its neighbourhoods (Luputa health zone)
assessments.evidence: Territorial-level trading town with PNC commissariat, ANR and administrative services; no reports of armed-group control since Kamuina Nsapu-era unrest in Lomami faded in 2017-2018. Insecurity limited to banditry and urban delinquency.

units.CD8104-luilu-2: Part 2 of Luilu territory (Lomami) covers the Wikong health zone in the far south-west of the territory, a remote rural Lunda/Ruund area bordering Kapanga territory (Lualaba). No armed group is reported to hold territory there as of 2026; Kamuina Nsapu-related violence that hit parts of Luilu in 2017 subsided by 2018 and left no lasting armed control in this area. Order is kept by customary chiefs under sparse PNC posts, with the state reachable from Luilu/Kamiji and Kapanga; residual insecurity is banditry and local disputes. Live web research was unavailable in this run (search budget exhausted), so the assessment relies on background knowledge and the default-state-presence rule, with low confidence.
units.CD8104-luilu-1: Luilu territory (Lomami province), comprising here the Luputa, Kanda Kanda and Kalenda secteurs/health zones, lies far from the eastern conflict zones and has no known armed group holding territory. Luputa, the territory's main town and a large trading centre on the RN1/rail corridor near Mwene-Ditu, is under state administration with a PNC commissariat, ANR and limited FARDC presence. Kamuina Nsapu-related violence touched parts of Lomami in 2017 but faded by 2018 without lasting control. Residual insecurity consists of banditry, land and customary-succession disputes, and police abuses. Live web research was unavailable in this run (search budget exhausted), so the assessment relies on background knowledge and the default-state-presence rule, with limited confidence.
